description: Division and sqrt via shift-subtract on the 24-bit mantissa; rounding ops. Tests vs host.

description: Map f32 to the i32 parts and f16 to the i16 parts in rc_for_type so moves, spills, ABI, load/store, select, call work. Inline bitcast, fconst, fneg, fabs, copysign (sign-bit ops). No libcalls.

title: Support i64/i128 value types (ValueRegs limited to 4 byte regs)
description: ABI now returns multi-value/wide results via the implicit return area (sangoku-7qz.7), but i64 still fails with 'value type i64 requires 8 registers; this backend supports at most 4'. Needs 8/16-register value representation (ValueRegs/rc_for_type) before i64/i128 args/returns and ops can compile.

title: Lower load/store offsets beyond -128..127 and sub-word memory ops
description: Matrix: load/store with offset 300 is unsupported at every width (lower.rs bails when the offset is outside -128..127); uload8/sload8/uload16/sload16 and istore8/istore16 are unsupported. Needed for struct field access past 127 bytes and for narrow memory ops cg_clif emits for u8/i16 fields.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix rows load.offset, uload*, sload*, istore* ok; emulator round-trip for offsets 0, 127, 128, 300 and negative.
close_reason: Offsets beyond -128..127 fold into the address via Add16; uload8/16 and istore8/16 lower; sload* deferred to 7qz.3 (needs sign extension).

title: Lower trapnz/trapz and wide multiply-high
description: trapnz and trapz are unsupported for i8 (cg_clif uses them for assertions and bounds checks); umulhi/smulhi are unsupported at all widths. Wire traps to the same abort path as trap, and implement mulhi through the multiply helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix rows ok for i8/i16/i32; trap fixtures show the abort call.

title: Fill remaining i16 gaps (signed div/rem, min/max, abs, shifts, rotates, bit counting)
description: Matrix: i16 lacks sdiv, srem, smin, smax, iabs, ishl-var, ushr-var, sshr, rotl, rotr, clz, ctz, cls, bitrev, smulhi/umulhi and the overflow ops. imul, udiv, urem, umin, umax, popcnt, bswap, ishl-const work.
acceptance_criteria: Every i16 row in tests/coverage/lower.md is ok.

title: Lower overflow-checking arithmetic (uadd/sadd/usub/ssub/umul/smul _overflow)
description: Unsupported at every width in the matrix. cg_clif emits these for checked_*/overflowing_*/debug overflow checks, so core cannot compile without them. Implement for i8/i16/i32 using carry/overflow flags or compare sequences; wider types follow sangoku-7qz.9.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded emulator regressions against Rust's overflowing_* for edge values.

title: Fix i32 load/store register allocation crash
description: tests/coverage/lower.md: load.i32 and store.i32 with an i16 address panic in regalloc (machinst/compile.rs:77 'register allocation: SSA(VReg...)'). Reproduce with the coverage matrix functions; likely the LoadMem8 sequence for i32 defines a vreg twice or leaves it undefined (lower.rs i32 load/store arms).
acceptance_criteria: load/store i32 lower, covered by a FileCheck lower fixture and an emulator round-trip.
close_reason: Fixed; regression tests in tests/lowered.rs and lower fixture

title: Fill i8 operation gaps
description: The matrix shows i8 lacks bnot, select, imul, udiv/urem/sdiv/srem, shifts and rotates, smin/smax/umin/umax, iabs, popcnt, clz/ctz/cls, bitrev, trapnz/trapz and the overflow ops, while band/bor/bxor/iadd/isub/ineg/icmp/iconst/ushr-const work. Rust u8/i8/bool code needs these.
acceptance_criteria: Every i8 row in tests/coverage/lower.md is ok or has a documented reason.

title: ISLE and CLIF-level optimizations in the frontend
description: Evaluate cg_clif optimization settings at opt-level 0..3 on this target: inlining, constant folding, dead-code removal, avoiding 32-bit temporaries where 16 bits suffice, and keeping code size small for 32 KiB ROMs. Measure with the phase 2/3 fixtures; no semantic changes.
acceptance_criteria: Documented settings with before/after instruction bytes on representative fixtures.

title: Enable debug aids: MIR/CLIF/asm dumps per function and ICE reporting
description: Phase tooling (frontend, clif, lower) works per crate; add per-function filtering, a stable --emit to keep rustc ICE output out of the repo root, and error messages that name the unsupported CLIF op with its Rust source span so core failures are triageable.
acceptance_criteria: Failing core function reports Rust span plus CLIF instruction.

title: Provide compiler-builtins/runtime functions for the target
description: Libcalls emitted for mul/div/shift/popcount/float ops, memcpy/memmove/memset/memcmp, and panic/abort entry points need real implementations linked in phase 5. Decide whether to use the compiler-builtins crate compiled for the target or hand-written RGBDS helpers in the runtime; keep symbol names consistent with rgbds::runtime_libcalls.
acceptance_criteria: Every libcall the backend can emit has a definition; link step reports no undefined symbols for core fixtures.

title: Lower intrinsics core needs (ctpop, ctlz, bswap, rotate, saturating, ...)
description: Map core intrinsics in src/intrinsics to CLIF ops that sangoku-7qz supports or to libcalls; audit which intrinsics core uses and which are still unimplemented on this target.
acceptance_criteria: A list of used intrinsics with status; every one used by core compiles.

acceptance_criteria: dyn Trait method call and fn pointer call fixtures run in the emulator.

title: Handle wide scalar types in cg_clif (i64/u64/i128/u128/f64/f128/f16)

Route these through the representation decided in sangoku-7qz.9 so MIR using u64/i128/f64 produces CLIF the lr35902 backend can lower (or libcalls to compiler-builtins). Includes checked arithmetic and overflow intrinsics (add_with_overflow, mul_with_overflow, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: core integer methods (checked_*, wrapping_*, overflowing_*, leading_zeros...) generate lowerable CLIF for all widths.

title: Build core and alloc for lr35902 as a regression test

acceptance_criteria: Command and nextest test exist; failure count recorded in README roadmap.

acceptance_criteria: Calls with scalar pairs, aggregates by reference and sret compile and run in the emulator.

acceptance_criteria: Fixtures for string/array/struct statics with pointer relocations assemble and read back correctly in the emulator.

acceptance_criteria: core and alloc build for the target with no usize-width cfg workarounds; fixtures for max slice and array sizes.

Keep our changes as a small identifiable patch series on top of upstream, record the base commit, and add a check in tools/ that lists our commits and builds core (cargo build -Zbuild-std equivalent) so rebuild_toolchain.sh results are reproducible. title: Decide and implement representation for i64/u64/f64/i128/u128/f128

Write the decision, then implement legalization in ISLE or lower.rs for the ops core needs (add/sub/mul/div/rem/shifts/compare/convert/load/store/select) and softfloat for f64/f128.
acceptance_criteria: Design note in wiki; i64 and i128 arithmetic and f64 operations used by core compile and match host results.

description: i32 load/store arms exist in lower.rs but are unexercised; a hand-written load/store with an i16 address fails the CLIF verifier. Determine how the backend types 16-bit pointers (cg_clif pointer type) and add fixtures for i8/i16/i32 loads, stores, offsets beyond the -128..127 window, and stack slots.

Decide: widen iAddr to include 16-bit (preferred, so the verifier can stay on) or keep it off.

Needed for i64/i128/f64 and large aggregates; define and document the convention, including callee/caller-saved registers.

acceptance_criteria: Matrix entries supported; bounded emulator regressions match host.

Initial probe on 2026-11-06 for i32 found: supported iadd isub ineg band bor bxor bnot icmp(all) select iconst uextend(i8,i16) ireduce ushr-const; unsupported imul udiv urem sdiv srem ishl sshr rotl rotr smin umax iabs popcnt clz ctz bswap bitrev sextend, variable ushr. i8 and i16 have not been probed yet. Cranelift instruction support lives in the cranelift epic.

Add MIR/CLIF/emulator fixtures for multibyte strings, char boundaries, forward/reverse iteration.

The ASCII-only str/char changes (commit 2f668166f28) are a mistake: revert them so str is real UTF-8 and find compact Unicode table representations; correctness first, efficiency second. Integer/ops lowering is NOT here: see the cranelift epic.

Output: saved MIR artifact on disk that phase 2 can consume without re-running rustc. title: Add variable SM83 shift and rotate helpers by optimization intent
description: Implement the YES variable-count decisions from sangoku-mt4.4 for 16/32-bit shl/shr/sar/rol/ror. Prefer compact masked bit loops for size and unoptimized builds; byte chunks plus residual bit loops for speed builds. Small known count ranges may favor the compact loop. Apply CLIF width masking and preserve Rust checked-shift guards before narrowing the count. Include argument packing, register saves, CALL/RET and stack cleanup in final code-size/cycle comparisons. Reference tested loop and byte-loop candidates in tests/support/src/shifts.rs and wiki/audits/shifts.csv.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler selects helpers by existing optimization intent; bounded tests cover zero, byte boundaries, width-1 and oversized counts, negative inputs and live values. Verify stack restoration, bounded writes, full caller costs and Rust guard semantics; keep exhaustive runs explicit.

title: Specialize constant SM83 shifts and rotates
description: Implement the YES constant-count decisions from sangoku-mt4.4. For 16/32-bit shl/shr/sar/rol/ror use byte moves plus residual accumulator operations; use ADD HL,HL for i16 shl counts 2..7 where measured best. Preserve identity count zero. Add missing i32 shl, arithmetic shifts and rotates. Keep tiny sequences inline; evaluate helper sharing using complete call-site bytes. Audit fixtures: tests/support/src/shifts.rs and tests/fixtures/shifts; measurements: wiki/audits/shifts.csv. Prototype costs are not promises for allocated backend output.
acceptance_criteria: Actual compiler output passes bounded semantic, masked-count, live-value and ABI regressions. Compare final allocated instruction bytes and T-cycles against the audit and existing output; avoid exhaustive default loops.

title: Support 128-bit and remaining integer types/ops in codegen and core
description: Add i128/u128 lowering (add/sub/mul/div/shifts/compare), signed div/rem, arithmetic shifts, rotates, widening/overflowing mul, leading/trailing zeros, popcount, byte swap, bit reverse for i8-i128 as core requires. Replace impl_unsupported_wide_fmt (fmt/num.rs) with real formatting. Related: sangoku-9tk, sangoku-clp, sangoku-mt4.*
acceptance_criteria: core integer methods for all widths compile; bounded emulator regressions per op class match host results.

description: Replace every Python file in tests with Rust equivalents: SM83 subset emulator and RGBDS harness, all existing execution regressions, runtime/division/popcount audits, spill/popcount compiler checks and baseline generator. Preserve test semantics, timing/stack/write metrics, fixtures, seeded input reproducibility and JSON/CSV/provenance outputs. Integrate ordinary tests with Cargo and manual audit commands as Rust tools. Verify parity against current Python outputs before removal, update active documentation, run required quality checks, log and commit; retain unrelated dirty files.
notes: Completed Rust migration: tests/support is the shared host crate, 53 integration regressions plus two existing CLI tests run with cargo test, and six Cargo examples replace all audit/check/generator scripts. Removed all 14 Python files. Preserved MT19937/rejection-sampled seed sequences, flags/cycles/stack/write checks, JSON/CSV/report fields and artifact retention. Differential checks: seed-7 inputs/measurements agree, 49 ROM images identical, sample and all three full historical CSVs byte-identical, Rust and SDCC baseline outputs byte-identical at the same path. Exhaustive runs: popcount audit 342928, division candidates 309985, runtime division 149329, compiler spills 171498, compiler popcount 1918408 (2892148 total). Cargo Clippy/format/tests and pinned blank ROM smoke pass. Log wiki/log/2026-11-06-15-46.md; active commands wiki/runtime-audits.md. Root workspace explicitly excludes pinned compiler workspaces; unrelated fixture C, Beads JSONL and submodule edits preserved.
close_reason: All Python test helpers/tools replaced by Rust with preserved semantic/measurement parity, exhaustive validation, documentation and migration log.

title: Select native SM83 population count by optimization intent
description: Implement the YES verdict from sangoku-mt4.3. Use the table-free bytewise parallel-count sequence in tests/fixtures/popcount/swar.asm as the speed default, emitted with explicit target register constraints and scratch/clobber modeling instead of expanding sixteen generic AND/add/16-bit-shift steps. Prototype helper cost is 51 code bytes and 216 T-cycles including RET; the minimally repaired current compiler output is 211 bytes and 936 clocks. The sequence preserves HL, which permits retaining a live input there in the synthetic inline caller. Keep byte/nibble table candidates available as audit references rather than adding a mandatory aligned table. A compact 13-byte, 664-clock shift loop is the audited size alternative. The current cg_clif bridge maps every optimized Rust level, including level 2 and size levels, to speed_and_size; do not infer a size-specific request from that flag alone. Keep table-free parallel counting as the default and document any separately propagated size intent. Fix the general post-allocation spill/reload bug separately in sangoku-7em; replacing this one expansion must not hide it. Detailed results and limits are recorded in wiki/audits/popcount16.md.
acceptance_criteria: Rebuild the pinned backend and compile actual Rust ctpop/count_ones probes, including u16 results, u32 zero-extension, and an input used again afterward. Execute all 65536 u16 inputs plus register-pressure/spill contexts; preserve SSA input values, stack and ABI behavior. Report actual compiler-emitted code/cycles and spills rather than treating hand-written prototype counts as guaranteed. Document default versus size policy, run backend and ROM smoke gates, and update the roadmap.

# SM83 shifts and rotates audit

`sangoku-mt4.4` recommends constant specialization and optimization-dependent
variable helpers. This audit changes no production lowering or runtime code.
Implementation follows in `sangoku-9tk` (constants) and `sangoku-clp` (variables).

Run the bounded comparison with:

```bash
cargo run --example audit-shifts -- --artifacts build/shift-audit-fast \
  --output build/shift-audit-fast/results.json
```

Defaults cover counts 0, 1, 8 and width-1, four explicit values and two seeded
random words, body/caller modes and the shortlisted candidates. More than eight
random samples requires `--full`; exhaustive checks require both `--full` and
`--exhaustive16`. Ordinary `cargo test` uses small representative matrices.

## Decisions

| Operation | 16-bit constant | 32-bit constant | Variable, both widths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Left shift | Replace: YES | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Logical right shift | Replace: YES | Replace: YES | Adopt: YES |
| Arithmetic right shift | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Rotate left | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Rotate right | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |

For constants, select byte moves plus residual bit operations (`lanes`). For
16-bit left shifts by 2–7, prefer the `pair` candidate using `ADD HL,HL`.
Zero-count identity: Replace: NO. Keep the identity operation.

For variable counts, select `loop` for unoptimized/size intent and `byte-loop`
for speed intent. The byte loop adds 28 clocks for counts below eight; a known
small count range can favor the compact loop even in speed builds. Mask CLIF
counts by width-1. Rust checked shifts need their full-width range guard before
count truncation; masked counts alone do not implement checked shifts.

Blanket outlining: Replace: NO. Inline tiny constant sequences. For helper
bytes H, per-use call bytes C and inline bytes I, outline for strict ROM savings
only when I>C and uses exceed H/(I-C). The CSV records the first saving use
count, including argument packing and live-value preservation. CALL/RET alone
adds 40 T-cycles.

## Measured costs

These body figures include RET in CPU T-cycles. Bytes are linked instruction
bytes. Candidates use the audit ABI; their costs are targets for implementation,
not guarantees about future allocated compiler output.

| Constant case | Current bytes / clocks | Selected bytes / clocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16-bit left by 1 | 7 / 40 | 6 / 36 |
| 16-bit left by 7 | 31 / 136 | 12 / 88 (`pair`) |
| 16-bit left by 8 | 35 / 152 | 2 / 20 |
| 16-bit right by 8 | 35 / 152 | 4 / 28 |
| 16-bit right by 15 | 63 / 264 | 7 / 40 |
| 32-bit right by 1 | 25 / 168 | 16 / 84 |
| 32-bit right by 8 | 81 / 392 | 10 / 60 |
| 32-bit right by 31 | 265 / 1128 | 14 / 76 |

Variable means below give equal weight to every legal normalized count, from
the retained full run. They are not averages over the sparse default cases.

| Width / operation | Bit loop bytes / mean clocks | Byte loop bytes / mean clocks | Byte loop min–max clocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 / logical shifts | 16 / 284.5 | 30 / 213 | 80–352 |
| 16 / arithmetic right | 16 / 284.5 | 32 / 217 | 80–360 |
| 16 / rotations | 18 / 344.5 | 32 / 241 | 80–408 |
| 32 / logical shifts | 28 / 836.25 | 44 / 385 | 128–648 |
| 32 / arithmetic right | 28 / 836.25 | 46 / 397 | 128–672 |
| 32 / rotations | 30 / 960.25 | 46 / 413 | 128–704 |

Manual helper body stack is 2 bytes for 16-bit and 4 for 32-bit, including the
return address and incoming arguments. Table ROM and owned scratch RAM are
zero. Complete caller, live-input caller, inline and inline-live measurements,
stack peaks and sharing thresholds are in [shifts.csv](shifts.csv). JSON adds
observed register changes; callers must treat AF/BC/DE/HL as clobbered unless
the final compiler ABI establishes narrower preservation.

The 16-bit input is B/C, output A/B, variable count A. The 32-bit input is
B/C/A/[entry SP+2], output A/B/C/D, variable count [entry SP+3]. SDCC uses a
bridge to its native ABI: 52 clocks for 16-bit, 84 for constant 32-bit and 132
for variable 32-bit. CSV native costs subtract that fixed bridge; compare
complete bridged callers for this backend rather than claiming native SDCC
is uniformly slower.

## Evidence and reproduction

Fixtures and compiler probes live in `tests/fixtures/shifts`; the executable
comparison is `tests/support/src/shifts.rs`. SDCC speed/size snapshots come from
the clean `/home/takashi/sdcc` revision 17147. Exact commands, source hash and
tool versions are in `tests/fixtures/shifts/provenance.json`. Optional `--sdcc
PATH` regenerates both profiles and checks normalized instruction parity.

The historical full report is `build/shift-audit/results.json`; retained
assembly/ROMs and compiler output are alongside it. Its CSV is committed here.
That run passed 2,204,465 candidate cases, 5,242,880 exhaustive constant-16
cases and 47,424 compiler executions. Reproduction, explicitly opt-in:

```bash
cargo run --example audit-shifts -- --full --samples 128 --seed 0 \
  --exhaustive16 --output build/shift-audit/results.json \
  --csv wiki/audits/shifts.csv
```

The final bounded run passed 1,968 candidate and 252 compiler executions,
plus 72 actual Rust shift/guard probes, with zero errors. Coverage includes
sign bits, byte boundaries, width-1, oversized masked counts, live inputs,
restored SP, return frames and stack-only writes. Rust guarded payload/validity
probes include count 65536; full core Option-return ABI remains untested.

Supported native CLIF outputs are assembled and byte-compared to emitted
machine code. Missing compiler operations use the explicit `bits` reference.
SRA flags/timing and auto-indexed HL loads/stores have independent emulator
regressions. The emulator models flat-memory instruction timing, without
interrupts, peripherals or banking. See the [testing log](../log/2026-11-06-16-40.md).

title: Fix mul16 runtime operand byte order for backend ABI
description: runtime/mul16.asm treats B as lhs high and C as lhs low, but the backend ABI assigns lhs low to B and high to C.
